reader.title: Shooting of H. W. Wood
bases: Men lying in ambush fired shotguns at and wounded the teacher of a colored school after he ignored a written warning to stop teaching (A9).
The only account is the Sanford Journal item as reprinted in the Savannah Morning News (A9); no independent report was found.

summary.text: The shooting of H. W. Wood was an ambush in Florida in late October 1880 in which unidentified men fired shotguns at Wood, the teacher of a colored school near Sorrento, and wounded him.
The attack followed a written warning to stop teaching, and the Sanford Journal, whose report reached the Savannah Morning News, called for the attackers to be punished.
Wood was "engaged in teaching the colored school" on the Blackwater branch of the Wekiva, in what the Sanford Journal called the "Soriento neighborhood."
He had received a written warning to "desist from teaching," which he did not heed; the report does not say who sent it or give Wood's own race.
On a Thursday evening, described as "of last week" in the Journal's account, men lying in ambush fired on Wood while he was preparing or eating supper.
Three shots were fired, and large shot struck him in the thigh and the arm.
Because the Journal's issue date is not given, the attack can be dated only to late October 1880, most likely October 28.
Despite his wounds, Wood was reported to be continuing to teach.
No arrests, inquiry or prosecution appear in the coverage, and the attackers were not identified.
The only known account came from the Sanford Journal, which said it had the story from two men of the Sorrento neighborhood who visited on a Wednesday.
The Journal announced the news "with pain," named the attack "bushwhacking," and wrote that "for humanity's sake" it hoped the guilty would be "detected and severely dealt with."
The Savannah Morning News reprinted the item on November 4, 1880, without comment in its "Florida Affairs" roundup, between a St. Augustine bear hunt and a Tallahassee death notice.
No other white paper's version was found, and the Black press of the period is not in the collection searched.

accounts.label: Sanford Journal (via Savannah Morning News)
accounts.gist: Two men from the Sorrento neighborhood told the Journal that Wood, after ignoring a written warning, was fired on three times by men in ambush while at supper and wounded, but continued to teach.

framing.detail: The Sanford Journal called the news painful, used the word 'bushwhacking', and hoped the attackers would be 'severely dealt with'; the Savannah Morning News reprinted it without comment in its Florida roundup.

H. W. Wood, teacher of the colored school; his race is not stated
